title: Migratory Grief: The Ukrainian Experience in Germany
summary:
Human migration, triggered by political conflicts, environmental disasters, and economic inequalities, presents both opportunities and significant risks. Migration-specific stressors—such as separation from family members and the loss of material and abstract resources (e.g., housing, language, identity)—are increasingly recognized as “migratory grief.” This can lead to temporary or chronic mental health problems (Renner et al., 2024) and may fluctuate over time (Casado et al., 2010). Risk factors identified in earlier studies—such as gender, income, language proficiency, social support, and discrimination—can exacerbate migratory grief and increase the risk of depression, anxiety disorders, and PTSD among migrants (Renner et al., 2024; Alpysbekova et al., 2024; Yasenok et al., 2025).
Since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, approximately 5.9 million people have fled; of these, over 1.3 million Ukrainians have sought refuge in Germany (UNHCR, 2026). Nevertheless, the psychological effects of migration-related grief on Ukrainian migrants—both children and adults—in Germany have been scarcely studied to date, leading to significant gaps in knowledge regarding their needs and the effectiveness of support systems. The inclusion of children is also relevant because psychological distress is common among refugee children, and early identification can facilitate needs-based support (Catani et al., 2023).

interventions.name: Quantitative online questionnaire of Ukrainians living in Germany

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The following inclusion criteria apply to Substudy 1: 1. Individuals of Ukrainian descent (i.e., individuals who were born in Ukraine) 2. Living in Germany 3. Individuals who speak Ukrainian 4. At least 18 years of age 5. Informed consent. 
For Substudy 2, the study will also include individuals who meet the above criteria and are legal guardians of children of Ukrainian descent between the ages of 7 and 17.
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria apply to Substudy 1: 1. Individuals who are not of Ukrainian descent 2. Individuals of Ukrainian descent who do not live in Germany 3. Individuals under 18 years of age 4. Individuals with no knowledge of the Ukrainian language 5. Individuals who have not provided informed consent. 
For Substudy 2, individuals who have no children or who have only children under 7 years of age or over 18 years of age are also excluded.
